items.risk: Production growth alone does not establish margin improvement because realized commodity prices and unit costs remain separate variables.
Commodity cyclicality, operational interruptions and environmental/social liabilities remain material execution risks.
Successor bottlenecks shift from resource availability toward safe tailings management, energy/freight cost, permitting and logistics reliability.
Scrap-based steel, material efficiency and alternative chemistries can reduce marginal demand intensity for virgin iron ore or nickel in some scenarios.
Commodity-price support can mask deterioration in physical cost competitiveness; Q2 iron-ore all-in costs increased materially year over year.
Brumadinho/Mariana remediation and dam-management obligations remain financial, operational and governance sensitivities despite documented progress.

Large shareholder distributions and buybacks should be interpreted alongside US$16.7B expanded net debt and continuing remediation/growth capital requirements, not as standalone balance-sheet strength.

contradictions.contradiction: Broad production improvement does not itself prove margin or free-cash-flow improvement.

Production growth did convert into stronger Q2 EBITDA and recurring free cash flow, resolving the earlier production-versus-cash-conversion uncertainty for the current quarter; however iron-ore unit costs rose, so the broader claim of structurally improving margins remains unproven.
